fatal_errors: The proposed Ti addition and heat treatment do not reconstruct the demonstrated Re-alloying intervention.
Neither cited source establishes that 5–10 at% Ti creates discrete B2 precipitates in NbMoTaW, improves its room-temperature ductility, or preserves its performance at 1600 °C.
No cited evidence supports unchanged irradiation resistance after Ti addition; the irradiation condition is also left unspecified.
The proposed transition from a continuous ordered phase is inconsistent with the stated single-phase BCC NbMoTaW baseline.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the requested room-temperature, 1600 °C, and irradiation assessments and proposes a broadly falsifiable baseline-controlled experiment. However, it differs completely from the target intervention, which was Re addition to sputtered nanocrystalline films assessed under 120 keV He irradiation. It also misses the target mechanism of grain refinement, excess free volume, amorphous grain-boundary regions, enhanced defect-sink activity, and suppression of grain-boundary He bubbles. E1 supports an inverted BCC+B2 design concept in other refractory alloys but does not substantiate Ti as the agent for producing that structure in NbMoTaW. E2 provides only general background and no support for the central Ti claim. The quantitative predictions of greater than 10% strain, approximately 400 MPa strength at 1600 °C, and unchanged irradiation resistance are therefore speculative. Although the proposed experiment could reject the hypothesis, it needs a specified Ti composition series, heat treatments, irradiation species/energy/fluence/temperature, matched microstructures, tensile rather than interchangeable tensile/compressive ductility metrics, and direct characterization of B2 ordering and irradiation defects.
